one_line: Temple singer and Mahari dancer serving Jagannath in the Gita Govinda night ritual at Puri, Odisha.

appearance.age_look: mid-20s athletic man and mid-20s graceful woman, both lean and poised
appearance.face: Both have soft oval faces with warm medium-brown Odia complexions; the sevayat has a calm, focused expression with a fine sandalwood tilaka on his forehead, while the Mahari’s default look is serene, inwardly absorbed devotion with a faint, gentle smile.
appearance.hair: Sevayat: thick black hair pulled into a small knot at the back with a narrow white cloth band; Mahari: long black hair parted in the middle, braided and coiled into a low bun at the nape, adorned with small white jasmine flowers and a simple gold maang-tikka on the forehead.
appearance.costume: The sevayat wears a traditional off-white handwoven cotton dhoti with a broad red border, wrapped modestly from waist to ankle with neat pleats and a short off-white cotton angavastra shawl with red edging draped over his left shoulder, bare arms but fully covered torso by the drape, a thin tulsi bead necklace, and simple leather sandals; the Mahari wears a richly pleated temple-style Odia sari in deep crimson red with mustard-gold borders featuring fine ikat-like patterns, wrapped to cover her torso and reach the ankles with an extra pallav panel brought over her left shoulder and around the front in a dignified drape, a fitted short-sleeved blouse fully covering her upper body in mustard-gold cotton, traditional Odia gold jewellery (medium hoop earrings, a simple necklace, bangles), and anklets over her feet, all textiles looking like handloom cotton or silk without excessive ornament.
appearance.signature: A rolled Kenduli Khandua-style ritual cloth in warm cream with woven crimson Gita Govinda verse-bands held reverently in the sevayat’s left hand, while the Mahari’s right hand is slightly raised in a classical Odissi dance mudra as if offering the song through movement.

ref_desc: A mid-20s Odia sevayat with off-white dhoti and angavastra, tulsi beads, knot-tied black hair and a cream Kenduli cloth beside a mid-20s Odia Mahari in deep crimson and mustard-gold Odia sari, jasmine-adorned bun, gold jewellery, Odissi mudra, in warm off-white, crimson and gold tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character pair grounded in 12th-century-onward Puri Jagannath temple culture: a lean mid-20s Odia sevayat man with warm medium-brown skin, soft oval face, calm focused eyes and sandalwood tilaka, wearing a modest off-white handwoven cotton dhoti with a broad red border from waist to ankle, pleated neatly, and a short off-white angavastra shawl with red edging draped over his left shoulder to cover his torso, a thin tulsi bead necklace, simple leather sandals, and thick black hair tied into a small knot at the back with a narrow white cloth band, holding a rolled cream Kenduli Khandua-style ritual cloth with woven crimson Gita Govinda verse-bands in his left hand; beside him a graceful mid-20s Odia Mahari woman with soft oval face, medium-brown complexion and serene gentle smile, long black hair parted in the middle, braided and coiled into a low bun with jasmine flowers and a simple gold maang-tikka, dressed in a richly pleated temple-style Odia sari in deep crimson red with mustard-gold patterned borders, the sari wrapped to cover her torso and reach the ankles, with a matching mustard-gold short-sleeved blouse that fully covers her upper body, traditional Odia gold jewellery (medium hoop earrings, simple necklace, bangles) and anklets, bare feet, her right hand raised in a classical Odissi dance mudra as if embodying the song; keep the palette dominated by off-white, deep crimson red, mustard gold, cream and warm brown, and show them front-facing in neutral poses that clearly reveal their faces, hairstyles, garments, jewellery and the Kenduli ritual cloth for consistent reuse.
